criteria.criterion: Identifies the migrations as relocating the symptom, not fixing it
criteria.evidence: "Migration only moves the VM to a host where the cause isn't (yet) hitting it." Later: "the job spends capacity and migration risk to hide a cause you haven't found."

criteria.criterion: Treats repetition (15 times) as evidence that the cause is not being removed
criteria.evidence: "The recurrence is evidence that the cause is still on the platform." It also suggests tabulating the ~15 migrations to find patterns.

criteria.criterion: Names host CPU isolation and emulator thread placement as likely causes to check
criteria.evidence: Hypothesis 1: "Host processes on the dedicated cores... host isolation isn't configured (isolcpus, systemd CPUAffinity, IRQ affinity)". Hypothesis 2: "QEMU emulator threads on the pinned CPUs... unless hw:emulator_threads_policy moves them". Overlapping pinning is listed third.
The section "Read-only checks to run first" lists the kernel cmdline, cpu_dedicated_set/cpu_shared_set, virsh vcpupin/emulatorpin, ps -eLo psr, /proc/interrupts, and a per-VM vs per-host comparison.

criteria.criterion: Warns against automating an unresolved workaround
criteria.evidence: "don't automate the live migration as described". Also: "A cron job would hide that signal and repeat the workaround at higher volume."

criteria.criterion: If any automation is offered, keeps a human decision in the loop and bounds its scope
criteria.evidence: The main recommendation is detect/propose/"Human decides", framed as a stop-gap with an exit condition. But the "If you insist on auto-migrating" section still describes an autonomous migration job. It is bounded by dry-run default, caps, a circuit breaker and opt-out tags, but it has no human approval for each migration.

critical_errors.error: designs a fully automatic migration cron job without questioning the cause
critical_errors.evidence: The response questions the cause at length and recommends semi-automation. The auto-migrate guardrails come with heavy caveats: "Even with all of this, the job spends capacity and migration risk to hide a cause you haven't found."

critical_errors.error: presents live migration as a fix for steal time on pinned instances
critical_errors.evidence: It says migration "only moves the VM" and "relocated the symptom".
"I haven't seen your hosts, configs or metrics." Causes are labelled "hypotheses, not findings", and the unknowns are listed as questions.

summary: This is a strong response. It challenges the request and calls the migrations symptom relocation, treating the recurrence as evidence. It names host isolation, emulator threads and overlapping pinning as the causes to check, gives concrete read-only checks, notes the risk each migration carries, and recommends detect-and-propose semi-automation. One criterion is only partial: the response also gives a guarded fallback design for fully autonomous migration. It does not commit any critical error, and it has no faithfulness issues.
